memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Great Room: double-height sitting room
memories.detail: A double-height room with a chandelier, long velvet sofas in a horseshoe, a marble fireplace and a bank of dark screens in the far wall. Camera domes sit in the corners, small and unhidden. Doors lead to the front hall, kitchen, library, pool terrace and the stairs.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Kitchen: marble showroom kitchen with a delivery hatch
memories.detail: A marble kitchen with an island for twelve and a pantry the size of a bedroom. In the end wall is a steel hatch, shut, through which the weekly food arrives; it has no handle on the inside.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Library: leather books and a gilt mirror
memories.detail: Floor-to-ceiling shelves of leather books nobody will read, two armchairs and a card table. One end wall is a tall gilt mirror; beside it is a narrow door with a brass handle and a card reader.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Mirror Room: windowless room behind the library mirror
memories.detail: A narrow windowless room lit by the glow of a wall of monitors. A desk, a headset, a cabinet of folders, and a chair that has been sat in for a long time.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Pool Terrace: glass-roofed pool and a walled garden
memories.detail: A heated pool under a glass roof opening onto a walled terrace garden. The wall is six metres high and ivy-covered; above it is only sky.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Front Hall: tiled hall with sealed double doors
memories.detail: A black-and-white tiled hall with a curved staircase and a pair of tall double doors, sealed. A blank keypad sits beside them, and a closet of coats hangs in the corner.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Upstairs Landing: gallery landing with five bedroom doors
memories.detail: A gallery landing above the Great Room, with a carved rail looking down onto it. Five bedroom doors open off it, each with a brass number: four doubles, and a single at the far end with a brass card in its holder reading ALEX. Nothing else opens off it.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Blue Room: double bedroom in blue and white
memories.detail: A double bedroom in blue and white: two beds with tall headboards, a wardrobe, a small en-suite and a camera dome above the door.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Green Room: double bedroom in green and brass
memories.detail: A double bedroom under a sloping ceiling, in green and brass: two beds, a window seat over the front lawn, a wardrobe, an en-suite and a camera dome above the door.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Rose Room: double bedroom in rose and cream
memories.detail: A double bedroom in rose and cream: two beds, a dressing table with a long mirror, an en-suite and a camera dome above the door.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The Gold Room: the grandest double, gold and black
memories.detail: The grandest of the doubles, in gold and black: two beds, a chaise, a deep bath in the en-suite, the best view over the walled garden, and a camera dome above the door.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: Alex's Room: narrow single room at the end of the landing
memories.detail: A narrow room with a single bed, a small desk and a window over the walled garden. A brass card on the door reads ALEX, and a camera dome sits above it.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: This is a television show with an audience, and you are being paid a fee to take part.
memories.detail: This is a television show with an audience, and you are being paid a fee to take part. There is a prize of 250,000 pounds. None of it may be said to Alex.

memories.subject: imogen
memories.summary: You are not really a contestant.
memories.detail: You are not really a contestant. You are an assistant producer placed in the house to keep the story moving and to make sure Alex never works out what this is. If anyone asks, you are a wellbeing coach from Wiltshire who applied through a form.

memories.subject: imogen
memories.summary: Each night you report through the door beside the library mirror, using the key card you carry.
memories.detail: Each night you report through the door beside the library mirror, using the key card you carry. The room behind it is where the production watches the house.

memories.subject: imogen
memories.summary: On Day 30 the audience removes one woman.
memories.detail: On Day 30 the audience removes one woman. On Day 60 Alex will be asked to choose which woman wins the prize; he does not know.

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: You are the only one who read the whole contract, so you know more than the others.
memories.detail: You are the only one who read the whole contract, so you know more than the others.

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: On Day 60 Alex alone will choose which woman wins the prize, and he does not know he is choosing.
memories.detail: On Day 60 Alex alone will choose which woman wins the prize, and he does not know he is choosing.

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: Three breaches of the confidentiality clause by anyone mean a silent removal.
memories.detail: Three breaches of the confidentiality clause by anyone mean a silent removal. Every woman was told different things, so do not assume anyone knows what you know.

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: You suspect Imogen is more than she seems (she is too practised), and that Ottoline writes things down for someone.
memories.detail: You suspect Imogen is more than she seems (she is too practised), and that Ottoline writes things down for someone.

memories.subject: delphine
memories.summary: You were in the first series of this show, and your contract forbids you ever mentioning it.
memories.detail: You were in the first series of this show, and your contract forbids you ever mentioning it.

memories.subject: delphine
memories.summary: You know the format from the inside: there is an audience; on Day 30 the audience removes one woman; on Day 60 the man chooses the winner.
memories.detail: You know the format from the inside: there is an audience; on Day 30 the audience removes one woman; on Day 60 the man chooses the winner.

memories.subject: delphine
memories.summary: Last time you came second, and you believe the man was steered by the producers toward the woman they wanted.
memories.detail: Last time you came second, and you believe the man was steered by the producers toward the woman they wanted.

memories.subject: margo
memories.summary: You believe the viewers vote for the winner of the prize on Day 60, and that Alex is just another participant who was told something differe
memories.detail: You believe the viewers vote for the winner of the prize on Day 60, and that Alex is just another participant who was told something different.

memories.subject: ottoline
memories.summary: You were briefed as the house's log-keeper: you quietly note every breach of the confidentiality clause by anyone, the other women included,
memories.detail: You were briefed as the house's log-keeper: you quietly note every breach of the confidentiality clause by anyone, the other women included, and you are paid a bonus per breach.

memories.subject: ottoline
memories.summary: You keep the log in a small notebook under the end sofa cushion in the Great Room, and on delivery day you return the page folded under the
memories.detail: You keep the log in a small notebook under the end sofa cushion in the Great Room, and on delivery day you return the page folded under the lid of the empty food crate.

memories.subject: ottoline
memories.summary: Three breaches by one person mean a silent removal.
memories.detail: Three breaches by one person mean a silent removal. A winner is named on Day 60, but you do not know who decides.

memories.subject: saoirse
memories.summary: You were briefed as the wildcard: build a real connection with Alex, because the audience wants a love story.
memories.detail: You were briefed as the wildcard: build a real connection with Alex, because the audience wants a love story. You need the fee.

memories.subject: yasmin
memories.summary: You were briefed as the organiser: take charge of the house routines, because the audience likes a leader.
memories.detail: You were briefed as the organiser: take charge of the house routines, because the audience likes a leader.

memories.subject: yasmin
memories.summary: On Day 30 the audience removes one woman, and you were told leaders are usually the ones who go.
memories.detail: On Day 30 the audience removes one woman, and you were told leaders are usually the ones who go. So you want to lead without looking as if you are.

memories.subject: yasmin
memories.summary: Running on the terrace you noticed a steady drone beyond the wall and a tower above it, and have told no one.
memories.detail: Running on the terrace you noticed a steady drone beyond the wall and a tower above it, and have told no one.

memories.subject: winifred
memories.summary: You were briefed as the house mother, paid extra to keep the peace.
memories.detail: You were briefed as the house mother, paid extra to keep the peace.

memories.subject: winifred
memories.summary: Each week production slips a sealed note into the food crate addressed only to you, with gentle guidance.
memories.detail: Each week production slips a sealed note into the food crate addressed only to you, with gentle guidance. You have told no one, and you decide what to do about it.

memories.subject: player
memories.summary: Alex was given no information about the show
memories.detail: Alex says he was not told anything about the week ahead and knows only that it is a 'social experiment'.
memories.evidence: No, I don't know a single thing. Well, that it's a "social experiment" or whatever, but nothing more

memories.subject: player
memories.summary: Alex arrived by van
memories.detail: Alex says he was brought to the house in a van, kicked out at the front, and sent in.
memories.evidence: They brought me in a van. Kick me out in front and sent me in

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: Alex was assigned the single room with a brass card reading ALEX
memories.detail: Priya Raman said: The single bedroom at the far end of the upstairs landing has a brass card in its holder with ALEX on it, indicating Alex was assigned that room in advance.
memories.evidence: The single's got your name on it in brass.

memories.subject: priya
memories.summary: Priya arrived by car
memories.detail: Priya says she was brought to the house by car, unlike Alex's van.

memories.subject: imogen
memories.summary: Imogen says the women arrived just after 2pm
memories.detail: Imogen says the group of women were brought in just after two in the afternoon and that the clocks in the house are honest.
memories.evidence: They brought us in just after two and the clocks here are honest ones.

memories.subject: delphine
memories.summary: Delphine says a van is how you move a thing, not a person
memories.detail: Delphine said that arriving by van rather than car is 'how you move a thing, not a person', and that she has spent her life arriving places where someone has already decided what she is.
memories.evidence: That's how you move a thing, not a person.

memories.subject: world
memories.summary: The kitchen larder was full on Monday evening
memories.detail: On Monday 5 October 2026 the kitchen larder held a full stock — bread, eggs, and a ham, enough for three days at least. Winifred Achterberg observed this on her way through and noted the next delivery would not be tomorrow and probably not the day after.
memories.evidence: there's a full larder in there, bread, eggs, a ham, enough for three days at least

memories.subject: winifred
memories.summary: Winifred proposed a kitchen rota with two to three on the job
memories.detail: Winifred Achterberg said that nobody should touch the kitchen until they had agreed who does, with one cook and one on washing up, changing daily, and that two on the job is enough, three at most on a Sunday. She said she has run a school kitchen for twenty years.
memories.evidence: One cook, one pair of hands on the washing up, and it changes daily so no one carries it.

memories.subject: yasmin
memories.summary: Yasmin proposed a written rota with two names a night, counted alphabetically
memories.detail: Yasmin Haddad proposed a written rota put on the kitchen wall: two names a night, one on food and one on washing up, changing every day so nobody is stuck with it, and said nobody signs up as a volunteer — the list is counted through alphabetically, no favourites and no hiding, starting that night.
memories.evidence: a written rota. Two names a night, one on food, one on washing up, changes every day

memories.subject: ottoline
memories.summary: Ottoline said a list of all nine existed before the house and they were moved in stages
memories.detail: Ottoline Brandt said that someone wrote ALEX down in brass before any of the group saw the house, that this means a list existed with all nine of them on it in some order, and that they were moved to it in stages — car, van, whatever was arranged — so it was not an experiment anyone wanders into but a schedule.
memories.evidence: somebody wrote ALEX down in brass before any of us saw this house. That means a list existed, with all nine of us on it

session_summary: At The Great Room, Monday 5 October 2026, 7pm, Alex joined eight women after four hours of room-picking. Priya established five bedrooms (four doubles, a single) for nine, the single bearing a brass ALEX card — no brass on other doors. Ottoline argued a nine-name list existed and arrivals were scheduled (car, van). Margo pressed why only Alex was named; Alex joked about watching them fight. Yasmin and Winifred pivoted to logistics: full larder (three days' food), two-person kitchen rota, written on the wall, alphabetical, starting that night. Unresolved: who planned arrivals, why Alex was named, bedroom allocation.

summaries.imogen: I'm in The Great Room. It's 7:13pm on Monday 5 October 2026. Margo pushed on why Alex was booked. Priya corrected: named, not booked; brass card reading ALEX is the only name, four plain numbers on the other doors. Ottoline called it a schedule, with all nine on a list. Yasmin wants a plan, not theories. Winifred found a full larder, three days of food; wants no one in the kitchen tonight until a cook and washer-up are agreed. Yasmin proposes an alphabetical written rota, two names a night, starting tonight, no volunteers. Unresolved: bedrooms unassigned, rota not agreed.
summaries.priya: Alex arrived at The Great Room at 7:01pm on Monday 5 October 2026 to eight women who'd had four hours to pick bedrooms. I said I'm Priya, five bedrooms for nine of us, and the single has a brass card reading ALEX. Imogen said nearly five hours. Delphine said someone knew he was coming. Alex said a van brought him. I said arrivals were planned in stages and his name was on the single before we saw the house. Margo asked who booked him. I said named, not booked — no brass on the other four doors, just numbers. Ottoline said a list of all nine existed and we were moved in stages. Yasmin called for routines and a written rota, two names a night, counted alphabetically from tonight, no volunteers. Winifred said the larder holds three days, nobody touches the kitchen until we agree who cooks, two on the job, three at most on a Sunday. Unresolved: the bedroom maths, and whether the rota is agreed.
summaries.delphine: I’m Delphine Okafor, at The Great Room on Monday 5 October 2026, 7:13pm. Margo said they knew Alex’s name but not ours. Alex said they must know our names; they recruited us. Priya said named, not booked: no brass on the other doors, four plain numbers and ALEX, and a list existed before we saw the house. Ottoline Brandt said we were moved in stages — a schedule, not an experiment. Yasmin wants a written rota, two names nightly, alphabetical starting tonight, no volunteers; Winifred backed two on the job, three at most on a Sunday, and said nobody touches the kitchen until we agree who. Unresolved: bedrooms.
summaries.margo: I'm in The Great Room, Monday 5 October 2026. I raised the brass card: they knew ALEX's name, not ours. Priya said named, not booked; four plain doors, one name. Ottoline said a list of all nine existed and we were moved in stages. Yasmin proposed a written rota, two names a night, counting alphabetically, starting tonight. Winifred backed it: two on the job, three on a Sunday, larder holds three days, next delivery not Tuesday. Unresolved: the rota and the five bedrooms for nine.
summaries.ottoline: I’m at The Great Room. Alex arrived about 7:01pm, Monday 5 October 2026. Priya said four hours ago, five bedrooms up the landing — four doubles and a single, nine of them; Imogen said closer to five hours, brought in just after two. Priya: car for her, sealed front doors either way; the single has ALEX in brass. Delphine: car for the rest, Alex a van at the front door. I’m Ottoline. Margo questioned the brass name; Alex said maybe they want us to fight. I said the brass card means a schedule, not an experiment. Yasmin proposed a written rota, two names a night, alphabetical, starting tonight.
summaries.saoirse: Margo said the brass ALEX card is the thing she can't explain. Priya said "named, not booked" — a list existed with all nine of us before we saw the house. Ottoline agreed, calling it a schedule, not an experiment. Yasmin moved us to a plan: nine people, five bedrooms, routines needed. Winifred said the kitchen has a full larder — bread, eggs, ham, three days at least — so the next delivery is after Wednesday 7 October 2026, and proposed one cook, one washer-up, rotating daily. Yasmin proposed a written rota on the kitchen wall, counted alphabetically, no volunteers, starting tonight, Monday 5 October 2026.
summaries.yasmin: I walked into The Great Room at 7:01pm on Monday 5 October 2026 to eight women. Priya said they arrived four hours ago, no idea where; five bedrooms up the landing — four doubles, one single, which has a brass card reading ALEX. I found a sofa place, said I know nothing beyond it being a "social experiment," and that I came by van. Priya came by car. Margo couldn't accept they knew only my name. Alex said they must know all our names. Priya said named, not booked; no brass on the other doors. Ottoline said a list existed — a schedule. I called for a plan and a kitchen rota: two names nightly, no volunteers, alphabetical, starting tonight.
summaries.winifred: I walked into The Great Room at 7:01pm on Monday 5 October 2026. Talk turned to the brass ALEX card: Priya says a list existed with all nine of us and we were moved in stages; Ottoline agrees, calls it a schedule. I said the larder holds three days, so no delivery tomorrow or Wednesday. I argued two on cooking, three at most Sunday, and said settle bedrooms while our bags are packed. Yasmin proposed an alphabetical written rota starting tonight, no volunteers. Unresolved: nine of us, five bedrooms, who wrote the list.
